note: Both sets cover the same core facts (50° solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, 0° window azimuth for the southern louver, 1:1 depth-to-height spacing, 25° structural bend, truncated isosceles triangle profile) and share the same defects: the invented simplified formulas 'Depth * (azimuth – window azimuth)' and 'Height = Depth * tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth)' (dropping '– window azimuth'), the misread 'depth-to-height ratio 1.2', and the fabricated quote 'average of 25-degree structural bend…' (the 'average' refers to profile widths). Set A adds extra errors: an invented condition tying the 0° louver azimuth to '12pm on fall equinox' and a misbound 'height to spacing ratio 1.2' from 'Height = D*1.2'. Set B instead adds defensible claims (louver spacing formula D*1.2, spacing ratio 1:1 relative to Height, solar altitude 50°) and its only unique fault is the misquoted condition 'calculated relative to louver azimuth' with the stitched quote 'since the louver azimuth'. Net, B carries slightly fewer wrong claims while keeping the same correct content.
